questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Reactive HTTP Resources”?
options: Reactive HTTP Resources means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Reactive HTTP Resources removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Reactive HTTP Resources should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Reactive HTTP Resources helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Reactive HTTP Resources helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Reactive HTTP Resources is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “The httpResource() API” in this lesson?
options: Assume “The httpResource() API” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “The httpResource() API” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “The httpResource() API” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “The httpResource() API” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “The httpResource() API” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “The httpResource() API” under Reactive HTTP Resources. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Reactive HTTP Resources”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
